note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Open seat (Sen. Daines withdrew at the filing deadline); four-way general.

MT-senate.statusNote: Open seat: Sen. Steve Daines withdrew minutes before the March filing deadline and endorsed Kurt Alme (R), who won the June 2 primary with 76%. Alme faces Alani Bankhead (D, 44% primary winner), independent former UM president Seth Bodnar (qualified by petition with 21,284 verified signatures), and Libertarian Kyle Austin. Bankhead and Bodnar each refused drop-out pressure before the Aug 10 withdrawal deadline, locking in a four-way general.

MT-house-1.statusNote: General election field from Montana's June 2, 2026 primary: Aaron Flint (Republican), Sam Forstag (Democrat). Open seat: Rep. Ryan Zinke is retiring and is not on the November ballot. Also on the November ballot: Nick Sheedy (Libertarian). An independent, Kimberly Persico, appears in one source only and is not listed here.

candidates.name: Kurt Alme
candidates.now: Attorney; resigned as U.S. Attorney for Montana in March 2026 to run
candidates.background: Great Falls-born attorney who served twice as U.S. Attorney for the District of Montana (2017-2020 and 2025-2026, both under President Trump) and as Gov. Gianforte's budget director and Revenue Department director; also led the Yellowstone Boys and Girls Ranch Foundation. Filed for the seat minutes before Sen. Steve Daines withdrew and endorsed him, then won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary with about 76%. Endorsed by Trump, Daines, Gianforte, and Sen. Sheehy; has never before run for office.
priorities: Make communities safer: prosecute violent crime and cartel drug trafficking
Protect the Montana way of life

cost.label: 'Deficit spending creates higher prices'; 'government spending and overregulation created these issues', answered with fiscal responsibility, tax relief, and cutting red tape (Montana Free Press election guide)

health.label: Backs the Rural Health Transformation Program, price transparency, and telehealth, recruiting clinicians 'rather than subsidizing health insurance companies' (Montana Free Press election guide)

housing.label: Increase housing supply by 'cutting red tape'; blames overregulation for housing costs (Montana Free Press election guide)

immigration.label: Primary victory pledge to 'secure our borders' (Daily Montanan)

taxes.label: Touts cutting taxes by $60 million per year as state budget director and a 'fiscally responsible budget' with strong reserves (Missoula Current)

safety.label: Top priority is making 'Montana communities safer': prosecuting violent criminals and drug trafficking 'all the way up to the cartels', paired with HEART Fund addiction-treatment support (Montana Free Press election guide)

repro.label: Endorsed by SBA Pro-Life America as one who 'can be trusted to be a true pro-life champion in the Senate' (SBA Pro-Life America)

democracy.label: Primary victory pledge to 'secure our elections' (Daily Montanan)

controversies.label: The American Leadership Fund super PAC boosting him has funded groups urging sale of federal lands; Alme says 'we need to continue to protect public lands' but declined questions on a public-lands agenda (Public Domain)

candidates.name: Alani Bankhead
candidates.now: Retired Air Force lieutenant colonel; co-hosts the 'Montana Matters' podcast
candidates.background: Retired Air Force lieutenant colonel and federal supervisory special agent who spent about 21 years investigating child sex crimes and, in her words, 'hunted terror networks, spies, and child predators across the globe.' Won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary with 44% in a five-way field. Refused calls from Democratic groups and former party chair Nancy Keenan to withdraw before the Aug 10 deadline, saying 'I already signed a blank check for my life to America 25 years ago', despite raising under $60,000.

health.label: 'We already know universal healthcare works': expand a TRICARE-style model to everyone, funded by cutting Pentagon waste; protect Medicare and Medicaid payments to keep rural hospitals open (campaign positions page)

housing.label: 'A Montana paycheck should buy a Montana home'; backs tax breaks for construction companies building affordable housing (Montana Free Press election guide)

immigration.label: Mixed: secure borders and fix systemic failures AND treat migrants humanely, drawing on her anti-trafficking career (campaign positions page)

climate.label: Mixed: 'Public lands stay public: period', with environmental studies before data centers, but also 'I'm for the Bakken and Montana energy' (campaign positions page)

education.label: Raise Montana's last-in-the-nation starting teacher pay and deliver the promised 40% federal share of special-education funding, up from 13% (campaign positions page)

safety.label: Runs on 'a record of putting child predators in prison' from 21 years of child-protection cases, emphasizing financial-crime investigation methods (campaign positions page)

repro.label: 'Reproductive freedom: trust people, not the government'; protect abortion access, citing Montana's constitutional protections (campaign positions page)

candidates.name: Seth Bodnar
candidates.now: Former University of Montana president (stepped down January 2026)
candidates.background: President of the University of Montana from 2018 to January 2026, when he resigned to run; Army Green Beret with two Iraq deployments, Rhodes Scholar, West Point economics instructor, and former General Electric transportation executive. Qualified as the first independent on a Montana federal ballot since 2022, with county officials accepting 21,284 petition signatures. Leads the field in fundraising ($3.2 million raised through June 30) and says 'I'm not worried about splitting the vote. I'm worried about earning votes.'
priorities: Bring housing and healthcare costs back in line with Montana wages
Defend public lands as common ground
Reform broken politics: ban congressional stock trading, overturn Citizens United

health.label: Will 'defend Medicaid Expansion and oppose reckless cuts' stripping coverage; backs telehealth expansion and rural workforce incentives to keep rural hospitals alive (Montana Free Press election guide)

housing.label: Mixed: build more housing by 'cutting red tape, using incentives in the tax code' AND prevent 'big private equity firms from buying up huge numbers of single-family homes' (Montana Free Press election guide)

immigration.label: Mixed: 'We need strong borders, we need to enforce our immigration policies' but 'without trampling upon the individual liberties of American citizens' (KTVH interview)

climate.label: 'I think we need fossil fuels', with renewables 'an important component of an all-of-the-above energy strategy' (Bozeman Daily Chronicle, Glendive campaign stop)

repro.label: Supports abortion rights, per NPR's profile of the race (NPR)

controversies.label: The University of Montana settled a sex-discrimination lawsuit for $350,000 in 2024; the 18 plaintiffs alleged wage, promotion, and opportunity gaps for women and the suit named Bodnar (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Kyle Austin
candidates.now: Pharmacist and owner of Pharm406 pharmacy in Billings
candidates.background: Fourth-generation Montanan raised on his grandfather's Hi-Line farm near Havre, which he now owns; pharmacist for 18 years with a University of Montana PharmD and an independent pharmacy owner. A former Republican, he won the June 2, 2026 Libertarian primary with 53% (1,819 votes). Hosts a weekly 'My Fellow Montanans' livestream and has challenged all federal candidates to open debates.

housing.label: 'Reduce the construction barriers', zero tariffs on building materials, support 'responsible logging and lumber mills' to cut home costs (Montana Free Press election guide)

taxes.label: 'Cut government spending so we can lower taxes'; 'we need to DOGE the government on a federal level and even on the state level' (Montana Public Radio Q&A)

democracy.label: Supports voter ID ('REAL ID'), comparing it to needing a driver's license, and opposes non-citizen voting (Montana Public Radio Q&A)

controversies.label: Won the Libertarian primary but 'was disavowed by the Montana Libertarian Party' (Wikipedia)
